title: Pat P NDE 21621
content: I had returned home after spending some time shopping with my mother. I put an item I had purchased at a garage sale in my storage area and went into the house. I suddenly had a severe crushing feeling in my chest. I grabbed the phone and sat down thinking I had done something unloading my purchase. I began to sweat profusely and at that time, I knew something was definitely wrong. I called 911 and explained the situation to the dispatcher. I began to get extremely tired and had to fight to keep talking to the dispatcher. I kept saying 'please hurry'. It seemed as though it took forever for the aid car to arrive. In reality, it was about 5 minutes. The medics loaded me on a gurney and into the aid car. I was still fighting to stay awake. I remember one of them asking if they could cut off my shirt. I thought 'Why do they want to do that?' At that point, I was looking down on myself watching the medic cut open my shirt. I wondered 'How am I seeing this?' Then I realized something was really wrong. The next thing I remember was being rolled into the emergency room.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes Heart attack Clinical death . I had suffered a heart attack.
elements.At what time during the experience were: I was in and out, but during the experience itself I was aware of my surroundings and what was happening around me.
elements.Did you encounter or become aware of any: Yes Just the medic attending to me
elements.What emotions did you feel during the ex: I was neither scared or upset. I guess curious would be the best descriptive word.
elements.Did scenes from your past come back to y: My past flashed before me, out of my control
elements.Did you have a change in your values and: Yes Not afraid of death any longer.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: The pain of the heart attack was the worst. The best is that I survived and was able to quit smoking.
elements.Have you ever shared this experience wit: Yes I don't know if they were influenced or not.
